title: Your first pull-up: Tom's eight-week plan
excerpt: Hangs, slow lowers and bands. The plan Tom has used to get more than fifty members their first pull-up.
content:
A first pull-up is one of the best feelings in the gym. Here's how we get there.

Weeks one and two: hang

Hang from the bar for as long as you can, three times, twice a week.

Weeks three to five: lower slowly

Jump to the top and lower yourself as slowly as you can.

Weeks six to eight: add a band

A band takes some of your weight while you build the strength for the real thing.

title: Deadlift basics: five things Marcus tells every beginner
excerpt: Bar over your feet, chest up, push the floor away. The deadlift is simpler than it looks.
content:
The deadlift is the lift beginners fear most and come to love most.

Bar over the middle of your foot

Start with the bar close. It should travel in a straight line.

Push the floor away

Think of it as a leg press, not a back lift.

Stand tall, then stop

At the top, stand straight. Don't lean back.

title: Boxing for complete beginners: what to expect
excerpt: Nobody gets hit, gloves are there to borrow and you'll learn a combination in your first class.
content:
Priya answers the questions she hears most from nervous beginners.

Will I get hit?

No. There's no sparring in class.

What do I need?

Trainers and water. We lend gloves and wraps.

Will I keep up?

Everyone works at their own pace. The bag doesn't judge.

title: It's never too late to start lifting
excerpt: Our oldest member started at 71. Why strength training matters even more as we get older.
content:
Strength training is one of the best things you can do for your health at any age.

Stronger bones

Lifting helps keep bones strong as we age.

Better balance

Stronger legs mean fewer falls.

Start where you are

Every exercise has an easier version. The coach will find yours.
